Subject: Intermittent latency spikes and token duplication on /v1/generate

Hi Neha / Marcus,

Over the last 40 minutes we've seen several requests against our streaming generation endpoint return duplicated tokens and an elevated tail latency (p90 up from ~120ms to ~1.6s). This started ~08:30 PDT and affected roughly 6% of requests for our prod API key. We attached a couple of example request/response pairs and a short trace IDs list.

Impact: some customer-facing chat sessions displayed repeated tokens which broke client-side parsing. We're holding a brief mitigation window but wanted to escalate to you for a root cause and planned fix.

Example traces attached: trace-1001, trace-1007
Attachments: examples.json (request/response snippets)

Can you confirm receipt and an ETA for investigation?

Thanks,
Tim
Senior Platform Engineer

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Sanders <tim.sanders@blueriver.com>
Date: 2026-09-01T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Intermittent latency spikes and token duplication on /v1/generate — technical findings and actions

Neha / Marcus / Tim — below is our technical summary, timeline, and concrete actions. Attaching the full diagnostic logs and the fix deployment log (blue_river_rca_v1.pdf, fix-deployment-log.txt).

Executive summary:
- Root cause: a race condition between node autoscaler drain events and our KV prefix-affinity logic caused stale KV references to be used in a subset of generation requests. This combined with a recent batching-path regression in the continuous-batching kernel produced duplicated tokens and higher tail latency for ~6% of requests between 2026-08-30 08:28 - 08:52 PDT.
- Impact: token duplication, increased per-request latency (p50 unchanged, p95/p99 elevated), affecting BlueRiver's prod API key.
- Mitigation: rolled back the batching kernel change, deployed an autoscaler fix that prevents draining before KV invalidation, and added an immediate server-side KV-invalidation on pool scale events.

Detailed timeline (PDT):
- 08:27:41 — Autoscaler initiated a scale-down for a GPU pool due to burst policies.
- 08:28:09 — First user reports of duplicated tokens (matches trace-1001).
- 08:30:15 — Continuous-batching kernel (v1.12.3) path observed to reuse hop indices leading to token duplication under certain interleavings.
- 08:39:02 — SRE applied a temporary mitigation (force full kv-cache flush on ingress for affected pool). Latency reduced but not eliminated.
- 08:46:00 — Full rollback of batching kernel to prior known-good build (v1.12.1) completed.
- 08:52:08 — Metrics returned to baseline; errors and duplication stopped.

Root cause analysis: two independent regressions combined (a) autoscaler ordering that allowed a draining node to keep serving requests until after KV state was rebalanced, and (b) a batching-path regression that assumed no mid-request KV invalidation. When both occurred the result was stale KV reuse and duplicated token emission.

Actions taken (completed):
- Reverted batching-path change (owner: runtime-team, Diego) — deployed 09/01 06:40 UTC.
- Patched autoscaler drain ordering to trigger KV invalidation before final teardown (owner: infra-team, Priya) — deployed 09/01 09:10 UTC.
- Added an explicit KV-invalidation hook on pool drain and on pod preStop (owner: runtime-team) — deployed 09/01 09:10 UTC.
- Added high-sampling tracing for BlueRiver keys for 72 hours for verification (owner: Neha) — enabled 09/01 09:20 UTC.

Planned actions (in flight):
- Post-deploy e2e verification runbook and Azure/GCP spot-checks (owner: Diego) — ETA 2026-09-03.
- Add long-term guardrails: canary evaluation for batching kernel changes and a rollout gating rule tied to KV-affinity metrics (owner: Platform Safety) — ETA Q4 2026.

Customer-facing remediation and verification artifacts included:
- blue_river_rca_v1.pdf (attached) — full logs, traces, and internal postmortem notes.
- fix-deployment-log.txt (attached) — kube deployment log with hashes and rollout timestamps.
- verification-runbook.md — step-by-step e2e verification we ask BlueRiver to run (or we can run jointly).

Compensation: Marcus, happy to coordinate account-level credit for the impacted window.

If you want a short live runbook call to walk the verification steps I'm available — recommend a 30 minute window tomorrow.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: BlueRiver: RCA delivered, verification steps, and next actions

Tim / Aisha — following up with the finalized customer package. Thank you for your patience while we completed the internal validation.

What's attached:
- blue_river_rca_v1.pdf: technical RCA, complete annotated timeline, and evidence snapshots.
- fix-deployment-log.txt: deployment hashes and rollout confirmation.
- verification-runbook.md: a concise checklist to run against your staging traffic (we can run this jointly).

Summary (short):
- Cause: race between autoscaler drain ordering and batching-path regression that allowed stale KV references to be used mid-request.
- Fixes: rollback of kernel change + autoscaler ordering fix + explicit KV invalidation hook.
- Verification: we've enabled high-sampling tracing for your API key and run the initial verification suite — results are clean; we'll keep the sampling window open for 72 hours.

Next steps and owners:
- Joint verification session: propose Wed 2026-09-08 10:00 PDT or Thu 2026-09-09 14:00 PDT — please confirm a preferred slot (Owner: Neha)
- Long-term guardrails and canary gating (Owner: Platform Safety) — update planned for Q4 2026.
- Account-level credit for the impact window (Owner: Marcus Lin) — Marcus will follow up with a credit proposal in HubSpot.

We realize this incident impacted your users and apologize for the disruption. As a gesture of goodwill we will provide a 25% pro-rated credit for the affected billing window while the team executes verification. Marcus will send the formal credit note and DocuSign if required.

Please let me know if you want the verification run run by us or for a joint session.

Best,
